Text

Wildfires have become more frequent in many regions over the last few decades. Although lightning causes some of them, most are started by people, often by accident. Hot, dry and windy weather allows flames to spread quickly, and firefighters may have only a few minutes to warn residents. Prescribed burns, which are carried out under controlled conditions, can reduce the amount of dry vegetation available as fuel. However, these burns must be planned carefully, since a sudden change in the wind could turn them into uncontrolled fires.

Text

A working smoke alarm can give a family the extra seconds needed to escape from a house fire. Even so, many alarms do not work because their batteries are dead or have been removed. Experts recommend that alarms be tested once a month and replaced every ten years. Everyone in the home should know two ways out of each room and agree on a meeting place outside. Once you are out, stay out: you must never go back inside a burning building to collect belongings.

When heavy rain hit the town last year, the fire department rescued more than two hundred people in a single night. Crews used inflatable boats because the main roads had already been closed. A spokesperson said that the flood would have caused more deaths if the warning system had not worked. Since then, the city has installed new sensors along the river. Nevertheless, officials admit that sensors alone cannot solve the problem unless houses are moved away from the riverbank.
